newsitem.title: UK: London gold follows silver higher at fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold follows silver higher at fixing.

text.p: Prices moved slightly higher across the precious metals complex on Wednesday afternoon, pulled ahead by trade buying in silver, dealers said.

A stock fall announced yesterday on the Comex and further news that the deliverable material from the Wilmington Trust warehouse was marked down 630,350 ounces to 58,782,969 ounces added to the more positive sentiment.
Gold was fixed at $381.35 versus $380.90 in the morning and $380.85 on Tuesday afternoon. It was the highest fixing since September 26.
The Comex December contract was up 30 cents at $383.70.
Technical analysts said gold could expect to make progress towards $384.00 if it could convincingly breach $381.70.
That resistance was showing itself to be resilient post the fixing with gold finding selling coming in as soon as the $381.30-$381.50 range was achieved.
"Everybody has been short and bearish for so long and yet the price hasn't gone down. This could be the first sign of a change today," one dealer said.
He added that gold could have the stamina to get back into the high $380s while silver aimed at $5.00 spot above which buy stops could accelerate progress.
But market sentiment in gold was still mostly bearish after prices slid to 18-month lows last week within a month-old downtrend, other dealers said.
"In the medium term, if there is a big price move, it's going to be lower," with $375 as the first target, one said.
Silver quickly developed a nine-cent range for the day after trade buying in New York sparked the move on the basis of warehouse drawdowns. It was last indicated at $4.93/$4.95
Dealers have cautioned for several days that silver was looking very prone to a volatile move in either direction, but more probably down despite being oversold.
"A nine cent range for silver is reasonably positive," one dealer said.
Silver had been even more somnolent than gold earlier opening three cents easier and struggling to hold around $4.85.
Platinum edged ahead by about $1.00 at its peak but had little appetite to go further following the gold fixing.
By 1430 GMT it was indicated at $384.50/$385.50 up 50 cents on the close.
Palladium edged lower while the other metals firmed to be indicated 75 cents down at $116.75/$117.75.
